name: Mita
tagline: Shinagawa in 10 minutes and Otemachi in 10 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Minato City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 10 minutes to Otemachi, 24 minutes to Shinjuku, 20 minutes to Shibuya and 10 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 3.4 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 4.7 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.4 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.6 m to 7.3 m, a difference of 4.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 4 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 17 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 愛育病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 芝公園かみやまクリニック, about 9 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Toei Asakusa Line and Toei Mita Line. Both lines are run by the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Toei Mita Line runs at 146% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 西巣鴨→巣鴨, which this station is not on. Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123%. Its busiest stretch is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which this station is likewise not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000 and 2LDK ¥380,000 to ¥390,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
